paragraphs.text: Wherefore leaving the doctrine of the first principles of Christ, let us press on unto perfection; not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
paragraphs.original: Διὸ ἀφέντες τὸν τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ λόγον ἐπὶ τὴν τελειότητα φερώμεθα, μὴ πάλιν θεμέλιον καταβαλλόμενοι μετανοίας ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων, καὶ πίστεως ἐπὶ θεόν,
paragraphs.translit: Dio aphentes ton tēs archēs tou Christou logon epi tēn teleiotēta pherōmetha, mē palin themelion kataballomenoi metanoias apo nekrōn ergōn, kai pisteōs epi theon,

paragraphs.text: of the teaching of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
paragraphs.original: βαπτισμῶν διδαχὴν ἐπιθέσεώς τε χειρῶν, ἀναστάσεώς τε νεκρῶν καὶ κρίματος αἰωνίου.
paragraphs.translit: baptismōn didachēn epitheseōs te cheirōn, anastaseōs te nekrōn kai krimatos aiōniou.

paragraphs.text: And this will we do, if God permit.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσομεν ἐάνπερ ἐπιτρέπῃ ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: kai touto poiēsomen eanper epitrepē ho theos.

paragraphs.text: For as touching those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,
paragraphs.original: Ἀδύνατον γὰρ τοὺς ἅπαξ φωτισθέντας γευσαμένους τε τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς ἐπουρανίου καὶ μετόχους γενηθέντας πνεύματος ἁγίου
paragraphs.translit: Adynaton gar tous hapax phōtisthentas geusamenous te tēs dōreas tēs epouraniou kai metochous genēthentas pneumatos hagiou

paragraphs.text: and tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the age to come,
paragraphs.original: καὶ καλὸν γευσαμένους θεοῦ ῥῆμα δυνάμεις τε μέλλοντος αἰῶνος,
paragraphs.translit: kai kalon geusamenous theou rhēma dynameis te mellontos aiōnos,

paragraphs.text: and [then] fell away, it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραπεσόντας, πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν, ἀνασταυροῦντας ἑαυτοῖς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παραδειγματίζοντας.
paragraphs.translit: kai parapesontas, palin anakainizein eis metanoian, anastaurountas heautois ton hyion tou theou kai paradeigmatizontas.

paragraphs.text: For the land which hath drunk the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them for whose sake it is also tilled, receiveth blessing from God:
paragraphs.original: γῆ γὰρ ἡ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπʼ αὐτῆς ἐρχόμενον πολλάκις ὑετόν, καὶ τίκτουσα βοτάνην εὔθετον ἐκείνοις διʼ οὓς καὶ γεωργεῖται, μεταλαμβάνει εὐλογίας ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: gē gar hē piousa ton epʼ autēs erchomenon pollakis hyeton, kai tiktousa botanēn eutheton ekeinois diʼ hous kai geōrgeitai, metalambanei eulogias apo tou theou·

paragraphs.text: but if it beareth thorns and thistles, it is rejected and nigh unto a curse; whose end is to be burned.
paragraphs.original: ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους ἀδόκιμος καὶ κατάρας ἐγγύς, ἧς τὸ τέλος εἰς καῦσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ekpherousa de akanthas kai tribolous adokimos kai kataras engys, hēs to telos eis kausin.

paragraphs.text: But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak:
paragraphs.original: Πεπείσμεθα δὲ περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀγαπητοί, τὰ κρείσσονα καὶ ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας, εἰ καὶ οὕτως λαλοῦμεν·
paragraphs.translit: Pepeismetha de peri hymōn, agapētoi, ta kreissona kai echomena sōtērias, ei kai houtōs laloumen·

paragraphs.text: for God is not unrighteous to forget your work and the love which ye showed toward his name, in that ye ministered unto the saints, and still do minister.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ἄδικος ὁ θεὸς ἐπιλαθέσθαι τοῦ ἔργου ὑμῶν καὶ τῆς ἀγάπης ἧς ἐνεδείξασθε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, διακονήσαντες τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ διακονοῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar adikos ho theos epilathesthai tou ergou hymōn kai tēs agapēs hēs enedeixasthe eis to onoma autou, diakonēsantes tois hagiois kai diakonountes.

paragraphs.text: And we desire that each one of you may show the same diligence unto the fulness of hope even to the end:
paragraphs.original: ἐπιθυμοῦμεν δὲ ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι σπουδὴν πρὸς τὴν πληροφορίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἄχρι τέλους,
paragraphs.translit: epithymoumen de hekaston hymōn tēn autēn endeiknysthai spoudēn pros tēn plērophorian tēs elpidos achri telous,

paragraphs.text: that ye be not sluggish, but imitators of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα μὴ νωθροὶ γένησθε, μιμηταὶ δὲ τῶν διὰ πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας κληρονομούντων τὰς ἐπαγγελίας.
paragraphs.translit: hina mē nōthroi genēsthe, mimētai de tōn dia pisteōs kai makrothymias klēronomountōn tas epangelias.

paragraphs.text: For when God made promise to Abraham, since he could swear by none greater, he sware by himself,
paragraphs.original: Τῷ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐπαγγειλάμενος ὁ θεός, ἐπεὶ κατʼ οὐδενὸς εἶχεν μείζονος ὀμόσαι, ὤμοσεν καθʼ ἑαυτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Tō gar Abraam epangeilamenos ho theos, epei katʼ oudenos eichen meizonos omosai, ōmosen kathʼ heautou,

paragraphs.text: saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Εἰ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ σε·
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Ei mēn eulogōn eulogēsō se kai plēthynōn plēthynō se·

paragraphs.text: And thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὕτως μακροθυμήσας ἐπέτυχεν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας.
paragraphs.translit: kai houtōs makrothymēsas epetychen tēs epangelias.

paragraphs.text: For men swear by the greater: and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.
paragraphs.original: ἄνθρωποι γὰρ κατὰ τοῦ μείζονος ὀμνύουσιν, καὶ πάσης αὐτοῖς ἀντιλογίας πέρας εἰς βεβαίωσιν ὁ ὅρκος·
paragraphs.translit: anthrōpoi gar kata tou meizonos omnyousin, kai pasēs autois antilogias peras eis bebaiōsin ho horkos·

paragraphs.text: Wherein God, being minded to show more abundantly unto the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath;
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ περισσότερον βουλόμενος ὁ θεὸς ἐπιδεῖξαι τοῖς κληρονόμοις τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τὸ ἀμετάθετον τῆς βουλῆς αὐτοῦ ἐμεσίτευσεν ὅρκῳ,
paragraphs.translit: en hō perissoteron boulomenos ho theos epideixai tois klēronomois tēs epangelias to ametatheton tēs boulēs autou emesiteusen horkō,

paragraphs.text: that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to lay hold of the hope set before us:
paragraphs.original: ἵνα διὰ δύο πραγμάτων ἀμεταθέτων, ἐν οἷς ἀδύνατον ψεύσασθαι θεόν, ἰσχυρὰν παράκλησιν ἔχωμεν οἱ καταφυγόντες κρατῆσαι τῆς προκειμένης ἐλπίδος·
paragraphs.translit: hina dia dyo pragmatōn ametathetōn, en hois adynaton pseusasthai theon, ischyran paraklēsin echōmen hoi kataphygontes kratēsai tēs prokeimenēs elpidos·

paragraphs.text: which we have as an anchor of the soul, [a hope] both sure and stedfast and entering into that which is within the veil;
paragraphs.original: ἣν ὡς ἄγκυραν ἔχομεν τῆς ψυχῆς, ἀσφαλῆ τε καὶ βεβαίαν καὶ εἰσερχομένην εἰς τὸ ἐσώτερον τοῦ καταπετάσματος,
paragraphs.translit: hēn hōs ankyran echomen tēs psychēs, asphalē te kai bebaian kai eiserchomenēn eis to esōteron tou katapetasmatos,

paragraphs.text: whither as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.
paragraphs.original: ὅπου πρόδρομος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς, κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἀρχιερεὺς γενόμενος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
paragraphs.translit: hopou prodromos hyper hēmōn eisēlthen Iēsous, kata tēn taxin Melchisedek archiereus genomenos eis ton aiōna.
